title: ChatFrame stream gateway and failure-tolerance patterns
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Summary:
We need a developer-friendly gateway abstraction for Python streaming chat that separates token-delivery from sideband event streams (tool calls, function signals, metadata updates). Current SDK helpers conflate fragments and make backpressure/retry semantics hard to reason about in hosted and Dedicated modes.

Goals:
- Provide a ChatFrame abstraction: a single ordered envelope that can carry one or more token fragments plus an arbitrary list of typed sideband events.
- Make idempotent resume and replay simple: each ChatFrame carries a monotonic watermark and a stable frame_id so consumers can checkpoint at frame granularity.
- Define soft-failure and hard-failure semantics for event decoding so callers can implement best-effort tool execution while preserving conversation state.
- Surface ergonomic retry/backoff helpers and recommended defaults for SDK clients to avoid duplicate tool side-effects.
- Emit telemetry hooks (per-frame latency, dropped frames, resume rate) to console dashboards for SLO monitoring.

Why different from prior designs:
- Existing iterator/chunk models focus on token streams; sideband events are often ad-hoc dictionaries. ChatFrame formalizes typed events and prioritization (e.g., function.call must not be lost, informational logs may be dropped).
- Frame-level checkpointing gives nicer developer mental model for restarts (resume from last committed frame instead of mid-token).

Proposed minimal API (Python):
- ChatFrame(frame_id: str, seq: int, tokens: str = "", events: List[Dict[str, Any]] = None, complete: bool = False)
- Gateway = AsyncIterator[ChatFrame] + helper methods: ack(frame_id), checkpoint(frame_id), soft_retry(backoff_policy), on_event(type, handler)

Behavior guarantees:
- Ordering: gateway yields frames in strictly increasing seq order per session.
- Delivery: at-least-once for frames; checkpoint/ack allows idempotent consumer progress.
- Resume: after reconnect, server will replay frames starting after last acknowledged seq.
- Event prioritization: events carry "priority" metadata (high, normal, low). High-priority events must be delivered before proceeding to next frame in-order. Low-priority events may be skipped on overload.
acceptance_criteria: Public doc: design RFC in Confluence with diagrams and explicit wire format
SDK: new ChatFrame class and Gateway async iterator implemented in py-sdk master
Examples: 2 sample apps (function-calling echo and streaming-assistant) showing checkpoint/resume and soft retry
Tests: unit coverage for ordering, resume, ack semantics and telemetry emissions
E2E: integration test against a stubbed server supporting replay and frame-level acks
Telemetry: dashboard chart for frame-latency and resume-frequency linked in ticket
design_notes:
Trade-offs and rationale:
- Frame-level granularity increases metadata overhead (extra seq/frame_id fields) but simplifies correctness for consumers and reduces user-surface for partial-token consistency bugs.
- We choose at-least-once delivery with client-side idempotency primitives rather than trying to guarantee exactly-once from the server; this plays well with function/tool calls where SDK exposes helpers to dedupe side effects (idempotency keys).
- Backpressure: Gateway should expose an awaitable .drain() that SDK integrators can call when local queues exceed threshold. This avoids unbounded memory growth in long-lived sessions.
- Batching vs latency: ChatFrame allows small token concatenation when system is busy (configurable, default: 32ms aggregation window) to improve throughput while preserving frame-level checkpoints.
- Security: frames may contain user-supplied metadata. Do not log PII at frame-level. Add sensitive_fields marker on events to redact in telemetry.
implementation_plan:
1) Draft RFC and on-call review (2d)
2) Implement ChatFrame dataclass + basic Gateway iterator (3d)
3) Add ack/checkpoint helpers + reconnection replay support (4d)
4) Add event typing registry and priority controller (3d)
5) Add backpressure/drain API and default thresholds (2d)
6) Write unit + integration tests and example apps (5d)
7) QA and roll out behind feature flag; monitor telemetry for 48h (2d)
8) Remove flag and promote to release branch when metrics stable
Notes: work can be parallelized: event registry implementation can be done before reconnection replay is complete.
